**Relative Position Index (`relative_position_index`)**
The input tensor is partitioned into non-overlapping windows to enable local attention.
Reshape input $x \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times W \times C}$ to $(B, H/W_s, W_s, W/W_s, W_s, C)$, where $W_s$ is the window size.
Permute dimensions to $(B, H/W_s, W/W_s, W_s, W_s, C)$.
Flatten spatial window dimensions to obtain windows $x_{win} \in \mathbb{R}^{(B \cdot \frac{H}{W_s} \cdot \frac{W}{W_s}) \times W_s \times W_s \times C}$.
Let $N_{win} = B \cdot \frac{H}{W_s} \cdot \frac{W}{W_s}$ be the number of windows.
Compute the index mapping for relative positions within each window.
Generate coordinates: $coords_h = \text{arange}(W_h)$, $coords_w = \text{arange}(W_w)$.
Create meshgrid and flatten to shape $(2, W_h W_w)$.
Compute relative coordinates: $relative\_coords = coords\_flatten[:, :, \text{None}] - coords\_flatten[:, \text{None}, :]$.
Permute to shape $(W_h W_w, W_h W_w, 2)$.
-   $relative\_coords[:, :, 0] += W_h - 1$
-   $relative\_coords[:, :, 1] += W_w - 1$
Map to 1D index: $relative\_coords[:, :, 0] *= 2W_w - 1$.
Sum to get final index: $relative\_position\_index = \text{sum}(relative\_coords, \text{axis}=-1)$.
**Linear Projection:** Compute $qkv = \text{Linear}(x_{win})$.
Reshape to $(N_{win}, N, 3, \text{num\_heads}, C/\text{num\_heads})$ where $N = W_s^2$.
Permute to $(3, N_{win}, \text{num\_heads}, N, C/\text{num\_heads})$ to separate Q, K, V.
**Attention Scores:** $attn = q \cdot k^T$.
-   Retrieve bias: $bias = \text{table}[relative\_position\_index]$.
-   Reshape/Permute bias to $(\text{num\_heads}, N, N)$.
-   Add to attention scores: $attn = attn + bias$.
**Softmax:** Apply softmax along the last dimension (key dimension).
-   Compute $x_{out} = \text{softmax}(attn) \cdot v$.
-   Transpose and reshape to $(N_{win}, N, C)$.
Reconstruct the full image from the processed windows.
Reshape $x_{out}$ from $(N_{win}, W_s, W_s, C)$ to $(B, H/W_s, W/W_s, W_s, W_s, C)$.
Permute to $(B, H/W_s, W_s, W/W_s, W_s, C)$.
The residual $\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial \hat{p}}$ is computed.
This residual (or the sinogram itself, depending on the specific variant) is passed through the DuDoTrans encoder/decoder blocks to refine features or predict corrections.
Ensure no overflow occurs if $W_h, W_w$ are large, though typical values (e.g., 7) are safe.
This makes it significantly more efficient than global self-attention for high-resolution images.
-   **Memory Complexity:** Memory usage is dominated by the storage of the attention maps within windows and the relative position bias table.
The bias table size is $O(W_s^2 \cdot \text{num\_heads})$, which is constant and small.
-   **Strengths:** Efficient local modeling, ability to capture long-range dependencies via shifted windows, and compatibility with differentiable tomographic operators.
